systems.name: Sol
notes: Sol follows a Solar System visual model at the author’s direction. Existing names are retained; unnamed planets keep their Sol numeral designations. Moon families remain part of the fictional atlas, including those of the two innermost planets. Orbital spacing and sizes are schematic.
systems.description: Sol resembles the Solar System with renamed worlds: four small rocky inner planets, two large gas giants and two outer ice giants. Eden occupies the Earth-like third orbit. Arcadia retains its provisional fifth-orbit placement. Orbital distances and body sizes are compressed for readability.

western.name: Occident Reach
western.subtitle: Western member worlds
western.description: Adrea, Athrys, Sutherland, Viery and Haldor form the western sweep of the supplied Alliance chart. Occident Reach is a proposed atlas division, not a documented administrative boundary.

sol.name: Sol Commonwealths
sol.subtitle: Capital and treaty worlds
sol.description: The central grouping around Sol and Eden includes Carver V, site of the Carver Accords, and the worlds of Acrius, Weiss 287, Blake’s Star and Freki. Sol Commonwealths is a proposed chart division.

acheron.name: Acheron Divide
acheron.subtitle: The Elysian approach
acheron.description: The upper approach toward Elysian space includes the DSC 346 black hole and Heimdall. Jotunheim’s Codex record places it in the Acheron Divide; the division’s extent and assignment of neighboring systems are proposed.

outer.name: Meridian Frontier
outer.subtitle: Eastern and outer systems
outer.description: Tessera, Bharask, Cassius, Hargrove, Torrin, Morrigan and Tenebrae occupy the eastern and lower reaches of the supplied chart. Meridian Frontier is a proposed atlas division; its name does not imply a connection to Meridian City.

aster.name: Aster March
aster.subtitle: Southern settlement arc
aster.description: A proposed southern chart region containing Aster, Hollis, Kepler 81, Redwick, Briar and Elara. All six systems and their settlements are creative atlas additions.

presentation.notesHTML:
UACS Stellar Atlas · v.04 · 134 CE

Scope and sources

The original 24 systems retain their relative positions from the supplied Cluster chart. Eighteen systems are proposed additions: three in each original region and six in the new Aster March. The Codex gives national totals of 253 systems and 42 member worlds; these are not the number of bodies in this first-pass catalogue. Every planet in the atlas has a selectable satellite family. The chart is schematic and does not establish travel distances.

Regional divisions

Occident Reach, Sol Commonwealths and Meridian Frontier are proposed chart divisions. Acheron Divide is documented in Jotunheim’s article, but its boundary and the assignment of nearby systems are proposed. All five regions share contiguous edges. Aster March is a proposed southern expansion with six new systems. Three further systems have been added to each original region. The source’s small secondary labels are transcribed provisionally where no article resolves their spelling.

Documented relationships

Karic orbits Eden. Varagandr orbits Jotunheim, which occupies Heimdall IV and has 78 moons. Heimdall is single-star. Carver V hosted the Carver Accords. The chart depicts DSC 346 as a black hole with DSC 346 B and V. Sokolov Observatory, and Weiss 287 contains New Dresden and Carson Station. Jotunheim’s prose calls it an ice giant, while its older infobox says gas giant.

Sol visual model

At the author’s direction, Sol follows the Solar System’s sequence of four rocky planets, two gas giants and two ice giants, with an asteroid belt between the fourth and fifth planets. Eden is Earth-like; Arcadia retains its provisional fifth orbit and now has Jupiter-like bands, while the sixth planet carries Saturn-like rings. Existing names and fictional satellite families are preserved. Sizes and distances are compressed, not physically to scale.

First-pass additions

Undocumented planetary slots, physical appearances, moon counts, station names and most orbital hosts are proposed. Generic planets use system-and-Roman-numeral designations and dimmer symbols. The 77 unnamed Jotunheim satellites use provisional catalogue names while preserving the documented count. Binary and triple configurations are proposed except the charted DSC 346 companion. Colors stay within natural stellar colors; they do not assert measured spectral classes. System views show vital satellites and major stations; planet views include every local moon and station.

Navigation

Index starts collapsed. The dropdown beside it opens a chart; clicking territory highlights it without moving the camera. Scroll or pinch to zoom, drag to pan, use Escape to return. Double-click a system or planet symbol to enter its chart; location names open Codex articles. Dossiers and Index collapse independently.

Label visibility

At normal chart sizes, overview names appear at 145%, or 110% for a highlighted region; planetary sublabels appear at 190%, or 150% highlighted. Dedicated regional charts use 64% / 80% for active names / sublabels, and 80% / 125% for neighbors. Narrow embeds increase these thresholds to preserve legibility.

Article embeds

Use ?view=widget&system=sol, ?view=widget&planet=Eden, or ?view=widget&region=acheron. Region keys: western, sol, acheron, outer, aster. Widgets keep Codex links. The MediaWiki importer may set window.SKYRIVER_ATLAS_QUERY before initialization. Full interactive embeds use ?embed=1.

Live planet names

Planet labels use their existing atlas names until a matching Codex article exists. Existing articles supply their current page titles; article moves and redirect chains update the labels and links. Checks run on opening, returning to the atlas, every minute while visible, and Refresh data. Cached page IDs follow later moves in the same browser even without a redirect. Keep a redirect at the original atlas title when moving an article so first-time visitors and other devices can discover the new title. Missing articles use the original atlas name; connection failures keep the last successful name. Planet identities, moon and station hosts, and old atlas links remain stable. A wholly separate article requires a redirect from the original atlas title.

Live article data

Dossiers refresh available images and infobox fields from the selected article. Missing pages or network failures retain the bundled atlas entry. All locations link to their intended Codex title, including articles not yet written.
